proposed.text: Under the IBC Section 506 combined formula, can the frontage increase (If) and sprinkler increase (Is) be applied simultaneously?

options.text: No — only one increase factor can be applied at a time, which limits the potential for maximizing building area.
Yes — both factors are additive in the formula Aa = At + (At × If) + (At × Is)
Yes — both factors are multiplicative: Aa = At × (1 + If) × (1 + Is), allowing for a compounded increase in allowable area.
Only if the sprinkler system is NFPA 13D; NFPA 13R does not qualify, which affects the applicability of the formula.

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Option C is the compounding trap — applying (1 + If) × (1 + Is) would produce a significantly larger result. For multi-story with If = 0.75 and Is = 2.00: additive gives 19,000 + 14,250 + 38,000 = 71,250; multiplicative gives 19,000 × 1.75 × 3.00 = 99,750 — a 425% difference. The IBC explicitly uses additive form.
